question.text: The half-life of a radioactive element is 10 hours. How much will be left after 4 hours in $1 \mathrm{~g}$ atom sample?

solution.text:
$t_{1 / 2}=10 \mathrm{hr} . \quad \mathrm{K}=\frac{0.693}{10}$
$4=\frac{2.303 \times 10}{0.693} \log \frac{1}{\mathrm{~N}}$
$\log \frac{1}{\mathrm{~N}}=\frac{4 \times 0.693}{2.303 \times 10}=0.12036$
$\log \mathrm{N}=-0.12036=\overline{1} .87964$
$\mathrm{N}=7.575 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~g}$ atoms
$\therefore$ No. of atoms $=7.575 \times 10^{-1} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23}$ atoms $=4.56 \times 10^{23}$ atoms
